# Release note style

Release notes are the maintainer's note to users, not an autogenerated report.
They are published on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/releases)
only. Use this guide when editing the `RELEASE-NOTES` region of a release
candidate PR.

The approach follows Immich and BentoPDF: explain the user-visible outcome,
credit the people who contributed, and link directly to the wiki instructions
people need after upgrading.

## Structure

1. **Opening paragraph.** Say what this release changes for someone running
   Pinchflat-ngx. Name the awkward behavior or missing capability and the new
   result. Plain words, short sentences.
2. **Highlights.** Group related changes under a few clear headings when the
   release is large. Skip headings for a small patch.
3. **Upgrade notes.** Call out configuration, database, file, job, or image
   changes and what the operator must do. Link the exact wiki guide and anchor.
4. **Fixes and reliability.** Mention the failure mode and the outcome, not just
   the pull request title.
5. **Contributor thanks.** Thank outside contributors and reporters by handle.
   Credit work accurately; do not claim authorship that is not yours.
6. **Included changes.** Keep the bounded generated list as an appendix. It is
   useful for traceability but it is not a substitute for the prose above.

## Container images and changelog

Keep the release footer in this format. Candidate preparation supplies it and
refreshes its version references while preserving the maintainer prose:

```markdown
## Container images

Use the versioned tags below or their moving aliases.

| Database   | Versioned image                                        | Moving tag        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| SQLite     | `ghcr.io/thebadfella/pinchflat-ngx:2026.11.2`          | `latest`          |
| PostgreSQL | `ghcr.io/thebadfella/pinchflat-ngx:2026.11.2-postgres` | `latest-postgres` |

Full changelog: [2026.11.1...2026.11.2](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/compare/2026.11.1...2026.11.2).
```

The versions above are examples. Use the previous published stable tag and the
candidate tag. Do not shorten the link label to “Full changelog” or replace the
image table with an inline sentence. Add build/runtime evidence only after it
has been verified. A correctly formatted handwritten footer is preserved;
stale tags or malformed formatting stop publication for review.

## Voice

- Write as the maintainer explaining a concrete change to another person.
- First person is welcome when supported by the work. Do not invent personal
  experiences, motivations, excitement, anecdotes, or user feedback.
- Prefer plain words. Avoid promotional openings, canned summaries, em dashes,
  and repeated "What's new / What's changed / What's fixed" scaffolding.
- Describe merged-but-unreleased behavior as upcoming, and keep instructions for
  the currently published version until the release is live.
- Remove empty template sections and `N/A` placeholders.

## Links

- Link the user-facing wiki guide, not a second manual in `docs/`.
- Preserve existing page URLs and anchors when guides are reorganized.
- Check links before merging. A code PR cannot publish the separate wiki
  repository's commit, so track wiki publication separately.
- Environment-variable definitions belong on the reference page; link to them
  from the release note instead of duplicating the table.

## Do not include

- Internal checklists, acceptance evidence, deploy instructions, tokens, or
  machine-readable release metadata.
- A raw autogenerated PR or dependency list as the whole note.
- Unverified test claims, invented release dates, or claims that a bot checked
  documentation when it did not.
- Shell snippets copied from untrusted input. Treat every note as literal text;
  the automation never executes note content.

## Example

```markdown
This release keeps a source's saved cutoff date stable across daylight-saving
changes, so scheduled downloads no longer shift by a day twice a year. Existing
sources keep their current behavior until you edit the cutoff.

### Upgrade notes

- The database migration adds a normalized upload-date index. Back up the
  database before upgrading, then follow the
  [upgrade guide](https://github.com/TheBadFella/Pinchflat-NGX/wiki/Upgrading-and-Rollback).
- PostgreSQL installations do not need a manual migration step.

### Fixes

- Retry authenticated thumbnails with the configured cookies instead of
  reporting a permanent failure.
- Show the actual publication date and download date when a cutoff rule skips a
  video.

Thanks to @contributor for the cutoff regression tests and to @reporter for the
clear reproduction.

### Included changes

- fix: keep cutoff presets across daylight-saving changes (#187)
- fix: retry authenticated thumbnails (#184)
```
